sections.title: Automation Manifesto — proceed by default
sections.content: Safe, reversible, auditable, already-authorized engineering proceeds automatically until a genuine human gate is reached.

sections.title: AI autonomy policy — when GPT continues automatically
sections.content: Routine safe work is AUTO/AUTO_WITH_CHECKS. Physical/destructive actions, secrets/credentials, trust ownership, protected merge/release and material security-policy choices remain HUMAN_GATE.

sections.title: Recoverable AI chat continuity and context health
sections.content: AI_WORK_STATE.md is the compact recovery checkpoint; GREEN/AMBER/RED context health remains heuristic rather than a fabricated exact context percentage.

sections.title: M13B physical result
sections.content: COMPLETE on the tested configuration. Corrected quick-check booted without old report Permission denied errors. Read-only lsblk showed the live USB mounted and internal 476.9G NVMe plus all four partitions with no mount points. Classification: OBSERVED on tested hardware, not universal/attested.

sections.title: M14 authenticated release signing
sections.content: CURRENT. The shared fail-closed validator requires exactly one top-level JSON object, exact canonical bytes and a closed field/schema set, and is tracked executable for clean checkouts. Detached Ed25519 signatures bind release ID/time, exact artifact filename/size/SHA-256, source/build identity and the trusted public-key fingerprint. The new regression rejects multiple JSON objects at the validator, signer and verifier, including a valid development signature over the invalid stream. Existing tampering, filename, key, signature and schema checks remain enforced.

sections.title: M14 development-test evidence
sections.content: LOCAL DEVELOPMENT EVIDENCE OBSERVED on 2026-11-09: all 14 positive/negative assertions pass using ephemeral development keys, and temporary test directories are removed on exit. The JSON-stream regression failed before the fix. CURRENT-REVISION GITHUB CI: NOT OBSERVED / CAPABILITY BLOCKED; the outbound proxy rejects api.github.com with HTTP 403. Add that hostname in environment settings while preserving existing domains, then inspect the exact final branch revision and successful completed signing self-test job. Git access or an eligible PR push is not itself CI evidence. Two unrelated pre-existing broader static failures remain documented. The Approved Release gate stays closed.

sections.title: M14 production key human gate
sections.content: Production release-signing private-key ownership/custody must be deliberately selected by the operator. The decision covers generation/holding location, backup/recovery, revocation/replacement, public-key distribution, compromise response and automation policy. No production private key may be committed to GitHub or placed on the general-purpose builder merely for convenience.

sections.title: M15 safe preparation without production authority
sections.content: The planned signed-UKI path has a Debian 13/systemd-ukify development design. It binds kernel, initrd, cmdline, OS release, uname and SBAT metadata, records UKI/section digests and requires negative tests. Only ephemeral DEVELOPMENT ONLY Secure Boot keys are permitted during this preparation. No firmware enrollment, target-disk write or production Secure Boot authority is authorized.

sections.title: Future modular Black Cat sessions
sections.content: Non-essential applications are planned as pre-built ready-to-run modules outside the immutable trusted core. A future icon/checkbox selector and safe presets choose only the software needed for the current session, and module selection is coupled to explicit least-privilege capabilities. Where practical, unticked modules are not mounted/exposed at all.

sections.title: Future external AI build workshop
sections.content: Natural-language tool creation should preferably build in a separate disposable VPS/VM workshop treated as untrusted. The workshop may design, compile and test but gets no trusted-core write authority or Black Cat production signing keys. Returned source/modules/manifests/tests remain potentially malicious until independently verified and capability-constrained by Black Cat.

sections.title: Pre-desktop AI boundary
sections.content: A lightweight AI interface may eventually help choose modules or request new tools before the full desktop is assembled, but only after a minimal authenticated Black Cat environment and capability broker are active. This does not authorize firmware/pre-kernel LLM execution.

sections.title: Release signing versus Secure Boot signing
sections.content: The M14 release-signing identity authenticates release metadata/artifact identity. The M15 Secure Boot/UKI signing identity authorizes executable boot artifacts under firmware policy. They remain logically distinct and must not silently share authority.

sections.title: Current Test Candidate versus Approved ISO
sections.content: The exact M13B candidate remains development evidence. No Approved Black Cat ISO exists yet; production release-signing authority is not provisioned.

sections.title: Zero-new-inbound automation policy
sections.content: Current M14/M15 work adds no inbound listener and no production secret to CI. The future modular/workshop design also does not authorize an inbound listener on the trusted core merely for convenience.

sections.title: Future native AI project automation in Black Cat Linux
sections.content: M26 remains future work after M25, backed by fail-closed repository policy, a sandboxed capability broker, modular session software and an external untrusted AI workshop for heavy/generated builds.

sections.title: Core trust chain
sections.content: Authenticated release reference -> verified USB image -> UEFI/Secure Boot -> measured boot/event log -> TPM evidence -> signed UKI -> dm-verity root -> immutable Linux -> RAM-backed state -> nonce-bound TPM Quote -> independent verifier -> attestation report.

sections.title: Mandatory lessons discipline
sections.content: Meaningful sessions update lessons and affected technical/decision documents; AI_WORK_STATE.md maintains compact handoff state and project_content.json is written last.

decisions.title: Reuse mature security components
decisions.text: Use Debian, UEFI Secure Boot, systemd UKI, TPM 2.0 and dm-verity rather than inventing replacement primitives.

decisions.title: Independent verification is mandatory
decisions.text: The target cannot be the sole authority deciding its own evidence is trustworthy.

decisions.title: GitHub is the canonical development workspace
decisions.text: Documents, source and the living JSON index are versioned in the private repository.

decisions.title: Lessons learned are mandatory output
decisions.text: Every meaningful session records lessons and affected documents before project_content.json is updated last.

decisions.title: Progressive hardening is mandatory
decisions.text: Temporary weaker controls must be explicit, bounded and later replaced.

decisions.title: Physical boot is observation, not attestation
decisions.text: Real-hardware success is scoped to the tested configuration unless stronger evidence upgrades it.

decisions.title: Current Test Candidate is separate from Approved ISO
decisions.text: Development testing and release promotion remain separate states.

decisions.title: Systemd is the sole Black Cat quick-check evidence producer
decisions.text: The root service produces evidence once; the login hook is display-only.

decisions.title: Automation Manifesto pre-pause check is mandatory
decisions.text: Safe reversible work proceeds automatically until a genuine human gate.

decisions.title: Automation must not add new inbound attack surface for convenience
decisions.text: Existing GitHub Actions remain the default automation infrastructure.

decisions.title: Root AI autonomy policy is the operational continue/stop authority
decisions.text: AI_AUTONOMY_POLICY.md classifies automatic work and genuine human gates.

decisions.title: Compact repository state makes AI chat dropouts recoverable
decisions.text: AI_WORK_STATE.md is the first-read recovery checkpoint.

decisions.title: M13B passes physical no-typing and internal-disk-default-unmounted gates
decisions.text: The corrected candidate passed on the tested hardware/configuration as OBSERVED evidence.

decisions.title: M14 release authenticity uses canonical Ed25519-signed metadata
decisions.text: Exact canonical release-manifest bytes are signed with a release identity distinct from Secure Boot signing. Ephemeral development keys may test mechanics; production key custody is a human trust-policy gate.

decisions.title: M14 manifest schema is closed and centrally validated
decisions.text: Generator, signer and verifier use one strict canonical/schema validator. Unexpected fields and ambiguous/non-canonical representations fail closed; schema extension requires an explicit future version.

decisions.title: M15 preparation may use ephemeral keys without creating trust ownership
decisions.text: Signed-UKI format/evidence/negative-test design can proceed with DEVELOPMENT ONLY ephemeral keys, but production Secure Boot key ownership/enrollment and firmware changes remain separate HUMAN_GATE actions.

decisions.title: Trusted core, selectable modules, untrusted AI workshop
decisions.text: Black Cat will keep non-essential software outside the immutable trusted core as pre-built session modules. AI-generated tools should preferably be built in a separate disposable workshop that cannot grant itself trust, alter the core or hold production signing authority; returned artifacts cross an independent verification/capability boundary before activation.
